e.etymology: An African American coinage that joins Mar-, as in Marcus and Marquis, to Shawn. Seattle Seahawks running back Marshawn Lynch carried it to its peak in the 2010s.
namesakes: Marshawn Lynch (NFL running back known as Beast Mode)

assoc.t: Marshawn Lynch, NFL running back known as Beast Mode

e.etymology: An American coinage of the 2000s made to rhyme with Jaden, Kaden and Aiden, with the fashionable initial Z. Zayden is the more common spelling.
A short form of Aaliyah, Arabic for exalted or sublime, taken up on its own after the singer Aaliyah's fame around 2000. It can also be read as a spelling of Leah or Lia.
A name of the Elena and Eliana family. In Greece Eleana is a modern form of Eleni (Helen) and Eleonora; in the US it also reads as Elena with the sound of Eleanor.
A respelling of Ellie, the pet form of Eleanor, Ellen, Elizabeth and other names beginning with El-, now given as a name in its own right.
A surname-style name that extends Kip with the place-name ending -ton, in the pattern of Kingston and Paxton.
From the surname Branch, itself from the everyday word, which English took from Old French branche. Baseball executive Branch Rickey, who signed Jackie Robinson, is the best-known bearer.
namesakes: Branch Rickey (Dodgers executive who signed Jackie Robinson)

assoc.t: Branch, the troll voiced by Justin Timberlake in Trolls

e.etymology: A short form of Hebrew Eliyahu, the prophet Elijah: my God is the Lord. It is a boys' name in Israel; in the US most bearers are girls, where it sits near Aliyah and Eliana.
A respelling of Kinsley, an English surname from a Yorkshire place name: Cyne, an Old English man's name built on the word for royal, plus leah, woodland clearing.
The Spanish double name Ana Lucía written as one word. Ana is the Spanish Anne, from Hebrew for grace; Lucía comes from Latin lux, light.
e.note: The first four letters spell anal, an opening for teasing; writing it Ana Lucia or Annalucia avoids it.

e.meaning: winner; one who fights for a cause
e.etymology: From the English word and surname champion, which came through Old French from Late Latin campio, a fighter in the field. As a first name it is a recent American word name.
Most often a clipped form of Israel, common in Brazil. In the US it has risen alongside Gael and Kael.

assoc.t: Raël, founder of the Raëlian UFO religion

e.etymology: A name used in the Dominican Republic, Cuba, Venezuela and other parts of Latin America, apparently adapted from English names such as Kendrick. US use comes largely from families with roots there.
A respelling of Jordan, from the Jordan River, Hebrew Yarden, from yarad, to descend. Crusaders carried its water home for baptisms, and children were named for it.

assoc.t: sounds the same as Jordan: Michael Jordan and Air Jordans
sounds the same as Jordan, the Middle Eastern country

e.etymology: A short modern name in the family of Kia, Kya and Kaia. It can also be a clipping of names that end in -kiah, such as Hezekiah and Zakiah.
e.note: Said KEE-uh, it sounds the same as Kia, the car brand.

e.etymology: The spelling of Veronica used across central and eastern Europe. Veronica is a Latin form of Greek Berenike, bringer of victory, later linked with vera icon, true image, for the saint who wiped Jesus's face.
A respelling of Ariana, a form of the Greek name Ariadne, most holy. In myth Ariadne gave Theseus the thread that led him out of the Labyrinth.
From the English word stony and the surname Stoney, given to someone who lived on stony ground. In the US it began as a nickname and is now given to boys and girls.
e.note: Sits close to stoned and stoner, so marijuana jokes are likely.

e.etymology: A respelling of Bailey, an English surname most likely from Anglo-Norman bailli, a bailiff or steward; for some families it referred to the bailey, the outer wall of a castle.
From Arabic sahar, the last stretch of night just before daybreak, borrowed into Persian as dawn. A separate Hebrew name Sahar, crescent moon, is used for boys and girls in Israel.
From Sanskrit vikrama, a stride and so prowess or valor. It recalls Vikramaditya, the legendary just king of Indian story, and is an epithet of Vishnu.
The Greek original of Nicholas: nike, victory, plus laos, people. Saint Nikolaos of Myra, the 4th-century bishop behind Santa Claus, spread the name across the Christian world.
A respelling of Jackson, the English surname meaning son of Jack. Jack began as a medieval pet form of John.

e.meaning: from Paisley, a Scottish town whose name may mean church
e.etymology: A respelling of Paisley, a town near Glasgow whose name probably goes back to Latin basilica, church. The town's weavers gave their name to the curved teardrop pattern.

assoc.t: paisley, the curved teardrop fabric pattern

e.etymology: A modern American coinage that puts the initial Z on the sound of Hailey, Bailey and Kailey.

e.meaning: meadow; also the star Vega, from Arabic for swooping eagle
e.etymology: Spanish vega is a fertile meadow, the source of the surname. As a first name it usually honors Vega, the brightest star in Lyra, whose name comes from the Arabic phrase an-nasr al-waqi, the swooping eagle.

assoc.t: Vega, one of the brightest stars in the night sky
Vega, the masked claw fighter in Street Fighter
Vincent Vega, John Travolta's role in Pulp Fiction

e.etymology: From Arabic kanz, treasure. Kenza is the North African form, a favorite in Morocco and Algeria and among families from there in France.
Esmée without its accent, from the Old French verb esmer, to esteem. Esmé Stewart, a French-born kinsman of James VI, brought it to Scotland in the 1500s as a man's name; it is now given to girls.
From an English surname taken from several places named Bowden, most from Old English boga, bow, plus dun, hill: a curved hill. It joins Bowen and Boden among recent American surname choices.
namesakes: Bobby Bowden (longtime Florida State football coach)
e.note: Said two ways: BOH-dun, or BOW-dun rhyming with how, as coach Bobby Bowden said his name.

e.etymology: From Arabic asra, to travel by night, the verb that opens the Quran's account of Muhammad's night journey. Isra and the Turkish Esra are close relatives.
From the English word bloom, a flower or the act of flowering, borrowed from Old Norse blom. Bloom is also a surname, in some families from Dutch bloem or German Blum, flower.
namesakes: Orlando Bloom (actor in The Lord of the Rings and Pirates of the Caribbean)

assoc.t: Bloom, fire fairy of Winx Club and Fate: The Winx Saga
